chapter: Growing up in the Thirteenth Ward
title: Marriage in 1946 and his wife's stroke
summary: They married in 1946 on his leave, celebrated 50 years, and she had a diabetic stroke in 1980 and needs constant care.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: What year were you married? I don't think you told me.
Yeah, when I went in the service. When I came on my leave, man, we hooked up. That's what I'm saying. We are the 15 of this.
That's right. You said you're going to be 50 years.

It was going to be. It was 50 years. It was 50 years. We had a party down at Ramada on St. Charles and Jackson Avenue. I had a big party, man. We had a lovely time. I wanted to bring you some pictures to show you. The cake and everything. I forgot.
50 years. I'm going to have a make-up.

Everybody talk about it, you know. But she took sick. She had a diabetic stroke in 1980. And left her that she's not able to do anything for herself. So someone has to always be at home with her. Someone always has to be with her. She can't do anything. If the house catches on fire, somebody can roll out the house, you see. Or get out the house, you see.
